name: Locust
what_it_is: Open-source performance and load testing tool where test scenarios are written as plain Python classes. Runs each simulated user inside a lightweight greenlet (gevent coroutine), enabling hundreds of thousands of concurrent users from a single or distributed cluster.
components: Master process — coordinates distributed test runs and aggregates results
Worker processes — execute user greenlets and report stats to master
Web UI — real-time dashboard for starting/stopping tests and viewing metrics
Locustfile — Python module defining User classes and tasks
HttpUser — built-in user class with a preconfigured requests-based HTTP client
TaskSet — container for grouping related tasks with optional weight and nesting
protocols: Custom (any protocol implementable via a Python client)
measurement: Worker count and worker status (distributed mode)
configuration: Spawn rate — users added per second (--spawn-rate / -r)
Wait time between tasks (between(), constant(), constant_throughput(), constant_pacing())
modes: Interactive web UI mode — start/stop/adjust load live via browser on port 8089
Headless CLI mode — fully scriptable, suitable for CI/CD pipelines
Distributed mode — one master + N workers spread across machines or containers
Single-process mode — master and workers combined in one process (--processes flag)
constraints: No built-in fault injection or chaos engineering primitives — must be implemented manually in task logic
No native support for non-HTTP protocols; custom clients must be written and wired in manually
Distributed mode requires network connectivity between master and all workers (default port 5557)
Locustfile must be a valid Python module importable by all worker processes; shared state across workers is not automatic
Real-time UI and stats aggregation add overhead — very high user counts benefit from headless + distributed setup
No built-in scenario replay from HAR or recorded sessions — scenarios must be hand-coded
notable_absences: No official docker-compose.yml in the repository root (404 on master branch)
No HAR or recording-based scenario generation
No native gRPC, AMQP, or database protocol clients (community plugins exist)
No built-in SLA assertion framework — pass/fail thresholds must be scripted externally
